contract: json is the exact expected text of the canonical variant-to-JSON conversion.
Decimals are fixed-point, never scientific, and keep their scale.
Floats and doubles carry the fewest digits that read back as the same value; two candidates of equal length equidistant from the value are settled toward the even digit.

Floats and doubles are laid out as Java's Double.toString lays them out: plain when the magnitude is in [1e-3, 1e7), scientific otherwise, always a digit either side of the point, an uppercase E, and no sign or zero-padding on a positive exponent.
For the 9 smallest float subnormals and Double.MIN_VALUE the JDK's own toString emits one digit more than needed; the shorter form here reads back as the identical value.
Temporal types are ISO-8601, T-separated, with the seconds field always present and the fractional group padded to 3, 6 or 9 digits.
Instants are normalised to UTC and spelled with a trailing Z.

cases.name: primitive_decimal16
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary says 1.2345678912345678e+16: it rendered the decimal through a binary double and lost the low digits. Ours is the exact unscaled value.

cases.name: primitive_decimal8
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary says 12345678.9, dropping the trailing zero. Scale is part of a decimal's identity, so it is preserved.

cases.name: primitive_double
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary says 1234567890.1234, the same digits laid out without an exponent. Java's layout uses scientific notation above 1e7.

cases.name: primitive_float
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary says 1234567940.0, which is Java Float.toString's pre-JDK-19 digits rendered without an exponent. Ours is the shortest form that reads back as the same float32; both parse to the identical value.

cases.name: primitive_string
cases.json: "This string is longer than 64 bytes and therefore does not fit in a short_string and it also includes several non ascii characters such as 🐢, 💖, ♥️, 🎣 and 🤦!!"

cases.name: primitive_time
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary says 12:33:54:123456, with a colon before the microseconds. Not a valid time format.

cases.name: primitive_timestamp
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary says 2025-04-16 12:34:56.78-04:00. The type stores an instant and the bytes carry no offset, so rendering one would invent it; normalised to UTC with the T separator.

cases.name: primitive_timestamp_nanos
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary spells the UTC offset +00:00; ours uses Z. Same instant.

cases.name: primitive_timestampntz
cases.dictionaryNote: Dictionary separates date and time with a space and truncates to .78; ours uses T and pads the fractional group.
